{{Short description|Mathematical ideal related to a modular curve}}
{{No footnotes|date=June 2020}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Eisenstein ideal''' is an [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] in the [[endomorphism ring]] of the [[Jacobian variety]] of a [[modular curve]], consisting roughly of elements of the [[Hecke algebra]] of [[Hecke operator]]s that annihilate the [[Eisenstein series]]. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Barry |last=Mazur|authorlink=Barry Mazur|year= 1977}}, in studying the rational points of modular curves. An '''Eisenstein prime''' is a prime in the support of the Eisenstein ideal (this has nothing to do with primes in the Eisenstein integers).

==Definition==

Let ''N'' be a rational prime, and define

:''J''<sub>0</sub>(''N'') = ''J''

as the Jacobian variety of the modular curve 

:''X''<sub>0</sub>(''N'') = ''X''.

There are endomorphisms ''T''<sub>''l''</sub> of ''J'' for each prime number ''l'' not dividing ''N''. These come from the Hecke operator, considered first as an [[algebraic correspondence]] on ''X'', and from there as acting on [[divisor class]]es, which gives the action on ''J''. There is also a [[Fricke involution]] ''w'' (and [[Atkin–Lehner involution]]s if ''N'' is composite). The Eisenstein ideal, in the (unital) subring of End(''J'') generated as a ring by the  ''T''<sub>''l''</sub>, is generated as an ideal by the elements

: ''T''<sub>''l''</sub> &minus; ''l'' - 1

for all ''l'' not dividing ''N'', and by

:''w'' + 1.

==Geometric definition==

Suppose that ''T''* is the ring generated by the Hecke operators acting on all modular forms for Γ<sub>0</sub>(''N'') (not just the cusp forms). The ring ''T'' of Hecke operators on the cusp forms is a quotient of ''T''*, so Spec(''T'') can be viewed as a subscheme of Spec(''T''*). Similarly Spec(''T''*) contains a line (called the Eisenstein line) isomorphic to Spec('''Z''') coming from the action of Hecke operators on the Eisenstein series. The Eisenstein ideal is the ideal defining the intersection of the Eisenstein line with Spec(''T'') in Spec(''T''*).

==Example==

*The Eisenstein ideal can also be defined for higher weight modular forms. Suppose that ''T'' is the full Hecke algebra generated by Hecke operators ''T''<sub>''n''</sub> acting on the 2-dimensional space of modular forms of level 1 and weight 12.This space is 2 dimensional, spanned by the Eigenforms given by the [[Eisenstein series]] ''E''<sub>12</sub> and the [[modular discriminant]] Δ. The map taking a Hecke operator ''T''<sub>''n''</sub> to its eigenvalues (σ<sub>11</sub>(''n''),τ(n)) gives a homomorphism from ''T'' into the ring '''Z'''×'''Z''' (where τ is the [[Ramanujan tau function]] and σ<sub>11</sub>(''n'') is the sum of the 11th powers of the divisors of ''n''). The image is the set of pairs (''c'',''d'') with ''c'' and ''d''  congruent mod 691 because of Ramanujan's congruence σ<sub>11</sub>(''n'') ≡ τ(n) mod 691. The Hecke algebra of Hecke operators acting on the cusp form  Δ is just isomorphic to '''Z'''. If we identify it with '''Z''' then the Eisenstein ideal is (691).
